service_boundary: Represents Cohere's hosted SaaS API, not Cohere models served by Oracle, Bedrock, Azure, or another partner and not private customer-infrastructure deployments.
regional_controls: Private and partner deployments may provide different residency controls; the public direct-API docs do not establish one customer-selected regional endpoint model.
retention_controls: Enterprise data commitments and account agreements govern input, output, and training-data handling; production customers should verify the applicable hosted-platform retention configuration.
routing: Customers select Cohere models and task APIs rather than upstream inference providers.
customization: Fine-tuning and private deployment options are available under separate eligibility and deployment paths.
strengths: First-party generation, embedding, and reranking APIs share one enterprise-oriented platform.
The service supports retrieval-heavy application patterns beyond generation alone.
tradeoffs: Deployment and data commitments differ between trial, production, private, and partner paths.
The direct catalog is Cohere-centered rather than vendor-neutral.

response_integrity.note: Scoped to the Model Vault Encrypted tier only. Its confidential-computing page states: "Verify before you trust: before any data is sent, the client verifies the deployment through remote attestation and refuses the connection if the environment is not genuine or is running unexpected code." The default API carries no signature or attestation.
response_integrity.scope: Cohere Model Vault Encrypted confidential-computing page, for the Cohere API

upstream_disclosure.note: The privacy policy states the operator collects the content: "we collect content you submit to the Cohere Products, and outputs generated by the Cohere Products". No subprocessor is named on a page this review could read.
upstream_disclosure.scope: Cohere privacy policy, for the Cohere API

credential_handling.note: The API offers no customer-supplied-key path: "To make a request to any model, you must pass in the Authorization Header and the request must be made through a POST request. The content of Authorization should be in the shape of BEARER [API_KEY]."
credential_handling.scope: Cohere API reference, for the Cohere API

cache_isolation.note: No prompt-caching feature or cache scope is documented in the chat reference.
cache_isolation.scope: Cohere chat API reference, for the Cohere API

vulnerability_disclosure.note: The security page publishes a bug-bounty programme: "The Cohere Bug Bounty program is designed to recognize the community's support in protecting our users' privacy and security."
vulnerability_disclosure.scope: Cohere security page, for the Cohere API

independent_audit.note: The security page names the API: "Our API platform is hosted on industry-leading cloud infrastructure and is SOC 2 Type II compliant". The report is behind a request-access control.
independent_audit.scope: Cohere security page, for the Cohere API
